analysis:
No security regression found in this batch. It only touches Sandbox CLI code (TB-013/A-019/T-061 context). Nothing changes the provider inference, attestation, key, cache or coordinator paths.

SandboxSetupProgress.swift (head 162-204): SandboxSizingPlan now parses an optional `disks` array from the installer's plan line. The parsing is typed and fails soft through compactMap, and the result is only used for display and sizing.

SandboxStatusView.swift (head 95, 189-203): adds display-only Work disk lines built from add-on status fields (path, state, detail). Add-on text has always been printed raw to the terminal, for example `detail` at line 79. Escape sequences in add-on fields are therefore not new; the add-on already runs as the owner (T-061).

SandboxWorkDisk.swift (new, 1-194): this is the main new surface.
- statfs-based volume probing (lines 50-69).
- APFS and ownership checks (72-83). These are advisory; the comment at lines 6-7 says the installer re-checks each disk.
- A privileged helper, enableOwnership (120-121), runs /usr/bin/sudo -- /usr/sbin/diskutil enableOwnership <mount> via posix_spawn (129-157). Executable paths are absolute and arguments are argv, not a shell, with `--`. Only stdio is inherited, via POSIX_SPAWN_CLOEXEC_DEFAULT (138-141). sudo asks for the password itself on the TTY. The mount point comes from statfs f_mntonname. No injection or descriptor leak is visible.
- shellWord (187-193) quotes correctly in POSIX single-quote style, and its output is only shown as a fix hint.
- candidates (173-184) filters for local, writable, non-hidden APFS volumes mounted at their own /Volumes path.

Unverified integration questions (callers are not in this batch):
- Whether setup asks the owner explicitly before calling enableOwnership.
- Whether the absolute --disk path is passed to install.sh as a separate argv element.
- Whether a TOCTOU between this check and the installer matters, given the installer re-checks.

Threat-model note: TB-013 does not yet mention the CLI invoking sudo diskutil, or that external work disks are owner-chosen peripherals. This is similar to the external-volume residuals in T-041 for cache storage. It is a documentation update, not a vulnerability.
